h1:
Udon Thani Desserts
Bakeries, Vietnamese Crepes & Cake Cafes
intro: Udon is a town where you can eat dessert all day. Start the morning with a crispy old-school Vietnamese crepe (banh xeo), swing by a fresh-baked bakery at lunch or a cool bowl of mixed Thai sweets, then settle into a cafe in the afternoon with a cake case holding a hundred-plus pieces. The town's Vietnamese heritage means Udon's desserts include things you'll struggle to find elsewhere. We've picked both the old-timers and the newer spots locals are actually going to right now.

blocks.html: When people think of Udon desserts, many only picture take-home gifts like moo yo (Vietnamese pork sausage) and naem nuang. But this town actually has sweets to graze on from morning till late, with a distinct Vietnamese accent — Vietnamese-descended families settled in Udon long ago, so the savory crepe is easier to find here than in other towns. The bakery and cafe scene has also taken off in just the past few years. We've ranked these by type of dessert, working from the old-timers to the newer spots.

items.name: Khanom Beuang Yuan Yai Daeng
items.blurb: The legendary old-timer of Udon. A thin, crispy crepe packed with shrimp, minced pork and bean sprouts, topped with grated coconut and spring onion, eaten with a sweet-sour dipping sauce. Yai Daeng has been making these for decades and sells out fast — go early, as it's usually gone by 2pm.
items.meta: Open 06.00–14.00 · come early before it sells out

items.name: VT Naem Nuang (dessert menu)
items.blurb: The largest Vietnamese restaurant in Thailand. People come for the naem nuang, but the Vietnamese desserts here are good too — savory crepes, fresh spring rolls and Vietnamese-style cold sweets. Great for finishing a meal or buying something to take home. There are two branches in town.
items.meta: Pho Si Road branch (behind Wat Photisomphon) · Mittraphap Road branch

items.name: Sri Fa Bakery, Thung Si Mueang branch
items.blurb: Isan's famous take-home bakery. The Thung Si Mueang branch is packed all day, with hot bakes coming out constantly — filled breads, cakes, cookies, and the purple-yam pastry that's its signature. Prices start in the low tens of baht and it boxes up nicely for gifts.
items.meta: By Televiz, Thung Si Mueang · open around 07.00–20.00

items.name: Kham Wan Ya
items.blurb: A spread of Thai sweets — tao tueng, bua loi, mixed bowls, shaved ice, soy milk and fresh milk, all cool and refreshing. Perfect when it's hot, and open late, so it's where locals sit down for dessert after dinner.

items.name: BEYOND CAFE Nong Prajak
items.blurb: A big cafe on the edge of Nong Prajak with a cake case holding a hundred-plus options, baked fresh daily. There are sliced cakes, dessert roti and breakfast too. Spacious and comfortable for a long sit, then a walk around the lake afterward.
items.meta: Nong Prajak area · open morning to evening

items.name: Sugar Rush
items.blurb: A sweets shop starting at 10 baht that's a hit with younger locals — small, cute pieces at very easy prices, so you can grab several to sample. Two branches: the Nong Prajak one opens in the morning, the other behind the regional hospital opens later.
items.meta: Nong Prajak branch 07.30–14.30 · behind regional hospital 09.30–18.30

items.name: Sweet Garden (Central Udon)
items.blurb: A dessert cafe inside Central mall — cute, bright and airy, with good-looking cakes and pastries at reasonable prices. Handy for a break while shopping or to escape the midday heat, with cool air-con.
items.meta: Central Plaza Udon Thani · open mall hours

items.name: Bellinee's Bake & Brew UD Town
items.blurb: A European-style bakery cafe in UD Town in the center of the city, with breads, pastries, cakes and coffee. Good for a rest or grabbing something before a train, since UD Town sits right next to Udon's railway station.
items.meta: UD Town (next to the railway station) · open mall hours

items.name: Molly Bakery (behind Udon Pittaya)
items.blurb: A newer bread shop behind Udon Pittayanukul School, with the smell of butter hitting you at the door. Loads of bread, and it gets busy when a batch comes out of the oven. Good for a morning grab to eat on the way or for a snack break.
items.meta: Behind Udon Pittaya School · come when a fresh batch is out

items.name: Monnaie Bakery
items.blurb: A health-focused bakery in town, leaning on wheat-flour-free, lower-sugar bakes — good for anyone watching their diet or avoiding gluten who still wants dessert. The flavor is better than you'd expect, and healthier sweets like these are still hard to find in Udon.
items.meta: In Udon city · check hours before you go

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: The old-school Vietnamese crepes sell out quickly — if you're set on Yai Daeng, go before noon to be safe. Fresh-baked bakeries like Sri Fa and Molly taste best right out of the oven, so ask the staff when the next bake is due.

blocks.html: The Vietnamese crepe (banh xeo) is nothing like the Thai khanom beuang with its crispy shell and sweet filling. The Vietnamese version is a thin batter pan-fried until crispy, then filled with savory shrimp, minced pork, bean sprouts and egg, folded in half like a crepe, scattered with coconut and spring onion, and eaten with a sweet-forward dipping sauce. It's a snack that Vietnamese-descended families in Udon have passed down for generations, working as either a light meal or a bite between meals.

items: Where to eat it — old-timers like Yai Daeng sell only in the morning, while VT Naem Nuang serves it all day alongside its other Vietnamese dishes.
How to eat it — eat it hot, straight off the pan when it's crispiest, with a moderate drizzle of sauce and some fresh vegetables on the side.
Taking it away — it boxes up to carry, but it's far better fresh; if you take it to go, keep the sauce separate and pour it on when you eat.

blocks.html: The bakery scene in Udon is busy, from big take-home names like Sri Fa to small new spots baking buttery bread all day. Most are in town within walking distance of each other, or inside big malls like Central and UD Town that are easy to drop into between sights.

items.name: Sri Fa Bakery
items.blurb: The big take-home name, with purple-yam pastry as its signature. Baked fresh all day and boxed up nicely.

items.name: Bellinee's / Sweet Garden
items.blurb: Bakery cafes in the malls, air-conditioned and easy to drop into for a break while you're out.

items.name: Molly / Monnaie
items.blurb: Small in-town shops for fresh-baked bread and health-focused bakes that Udon locals actually go to.

blocks.text: Dessert cafes — sit, chill and eat sweets in town

blocks.html: Plenty of Udon cafes are as strong on desserts as they are on coffee. A cake case with a hundred-plus pieces, like the one at BEYOND CAFE, is hard to find in other towns. The Nong Prajak area has several cafes clustered together, so you can stroll around the lake and drop in. If you want the full picture of Udon's cafe scene — chill spots and photo corners included — see our Udon cafe guide.

faq.q: Where's the best place for Vietnamese crepes in Udon?
faq.a: The legendary old-timer is Khanom Beuang Yuan Yai Daeng — a thin, crispy crepe with a packed filling, around 40 baht per box. But it only sells from morning to early afternoon and goes fast. If you're running late, try VT Naem Nuang, which serves Vietnamese crepes and other Vietnamese desserts all day alongside its full menu.

faq.q: Where should I buy Udon bakery items as gifts?
faq.a: Sri Fa Bakery's Thung Si Mueang branch is the famous take-home name — baked fresh all day, best known for its purple-yam pastry, starting around 19 baht and boxed up neatly to carry. In the malls there's Bellinee's at UD Town and Sweet Garden at Central.

faq.q: Which dessert cafes in Udon are good for a relaxed sit?
faq.a: BEYOND CAFE on the edge of Nong Prajak has a cake case with a hundred-plus options and lots of space — great for a long sit followed by a walk around the lake. If you'd rather be in an air-conditioned mall, there's Sweet Garden at Central and Bellinee's at UD Town.

faq.q: About how much do desserts in Udon cost?
faq.a: Bowls of mixed Thai sweets run 25–50 baht, Vietnamese crepes around 40 baht per box, and bakery items start in the low tens of baht up to cafe cake slices at 65–130 baht. Spots like Sugar Rush start at 10 baht, so you can buy several to sample for a budget of just a few hundred baht.

faq.q: Which Udon dessert spots are open late?
faq.a: Kham Wan Ya is open until around 23.30 and is where locals sit for a cool dessert after dinner — tao tueng, bua loi, mixed bowls and shaved ice — a light way to end the night.
